voice: Fourteen clue-bearing eavesdropping conversations in the established P2-08 voices, preserving flirtation, prejudice, vanity, suspicion, and plot information without phonetic ethnicity or national caricature.

entries.text: Countess, I hardly think that is likely. Secret societies of the kind you describe have not existed for hundreds of years.
I am only expressing my opinion, madam. I certainly do not claim expertise in secret societies.
QUITE so. My theory is as GOOD as anyone's, DARLING, and it comes from a RELIABLE source.
Oh? Who might that be?
There is a first time for everything, Countess. I still find your theory far-fetched.
What? Oh...I definitely think it is worth considering, Countess.
...so that is the arrangement, Countess.
No argument from me. The walls have ears around here--and so do certain reporters, if you follow me.
Certainly, toots.
The matter is not settled merely because you wish it so, Detective.
What's that supposed to be, some kind of diplomatic answer?
There I was above the excavation in the Valley of the Kings, with our foreman Mahmoud reviewing the day's survey, when a shout rose from the workers below.
Magnifique! A remarkable achievement, Dr. Carter.
And that is when you lifted it, correct?
I did not 'lift' it, you irritating little man. I brought it from the temple and presented it to the workers, who gathered around to admire the discovery and congratulate me.
That is difficult to believe, Dr. Carter. Egyptian workers have conducted archaeological digs with great pride for many years. I doubt they would exaggerate their admiration to such an extent.
No, I was not there.
Precisely. And when were you last in Egypt, Mr. Najeer? You speak with remarkable confidence for a man who has been away so long.
It has been several years.
If you will excuse me, I see someone with whom I must speak.
Yvette is quite a woman, is she not?
Yes. Miss Delacroix possesses a remarkable confidence. My wife has always preferred more conventional surroundings.
Miss Delacroix does have a gift for turning unusual surroundings to her advantage. I have found conversation with her unexpectedly memorable.
We Americans do produce a memorable phrase now and then.
I TOLD you to stop BOTHERING me, you tiresome bureaucrat!
Countess, I understand you were married to the museum's previous president.
Yes, DARLING, that is correct. Sterling Waldorf-Carlton was SUCH a charming man, and SO wealthy. My heart is an empty VOID without him.
It is difficult to lose someone you love. You were married only a short time, were you not?
Yes. I had only TWO short but charming months of MARRIED life with Sterling before he DIED.
And how long had you known him before the marriage?
We met only one CHARMING month before deciding to marry. It was LOVE at first sight.

I had been in this country only a few WEEKS when I met Sterling aboard an offshore casino ship. Drinking and gambling are quite LEGAL there, you know, and ALL the right people attend. Sterling simply SWEPT me off my feet.
Then Sterling must have carried a very large broom.
The MONEY does not MATTER, darling. There is an annoying PROBLEM with the estate. Sterling was changing his WILL when he died--to leave me MORE money, perhaps. I am SURE my ATTORNEY will settle it.
Ryan, I am finding it very difficult to keep my hands off you.
They are not important. YOU are the most powerful man here, my Ryan.
The doctor is old and weak. You are young...and strong.
Archaeology is such a MASCULINE profession. Breaking into ancient tombs with a sledgehammer, forcing open treasure chambers, handling gold artifacts... It is all very STIMULATING, no?
And it must be such a burden to bear this greatness. With so much pressure to perform, you must be perfect at all times.
Your problems are quite obvious, Dr. Carter.
But the Tutankhamen discovery is nothing beside YOUR achievement, surely.
I would LOVE to hear more about your work, Dr. Carter. Perhaps later tonight?
Oh, yes. Everyone will be here tonight, will they not? There is much to prepare before your exhibit opens tomorrow.
That sounds wonderful. Perhaps you would come to my office then?
It is very gracious of you to spare the time.
How shall I repay such courtesy? I know how busy you are, Dr. Carter.
I admire a man who speaks with confidence and knows precisely what he wants.
My household is orderly because my wife and I understand our responsibilities to one another.
Do not mistake Mr. Najeer's domestic opinions for those of an entire civilization. Egypt has contained many ideas over many centuries.
And are Egyptian men equally confident in more private matters?
Speaking for myself, I make it my business to be knowledgeable in every matter that concerns me.
I have certainly heard no complaints regarding my own...abilities, Miss Delacroix.
Miss Bow! I did not see you standing there.
A turkey leg sounds excellent. I will accompany you, Dr. Smith.
You are interested in great art, are you not? Then come with me this evening. I will give you a private tour of the Old Masters Gallery.
I promise you will not be wasting your time. You will enjoy it very much.
You ARE studying art at the university, no?
Then it is settled. I will give you the private tour shortly.
There is no need to thank me yet. I expect to enjoy it as much as you will.
The food is adequate. I eat very little; one must take care of one's figure.
Merci, Miss Bow. And your gown is...a little out of date, but charming nonetheless.
Well, well. Look what trouble dragged in.
Careful, O'Riley. I do not care for the way you say that.
Only by low-class individuals, O'Riley. Are you not worried about being seen with me?
I am a great patron of the arts. That is the sort of refined gentleman I am.
Of course I do.
Ah...is that the Countess over there? I must speak with her.
Well, you have become quite the society dame. I almost failed to recognize you with your clothes on.
Excusez-moi. Do I know you, sir?
Ziggy. Surely you remember me. Or are we pretending otherwise?
You must be joking. Perhaps you have confused me with someone else.
I am not joking. You are Yvette Delacroix. I would recognize you anywhere.
I am sure I do not know what you mean, Mr. Ziggy.
Ah. You are worried one of these high-hats will hear us. I understand. We can speak later.
